questions.stem: Why do transformers only work with alternating current (AC) and not direct current (DC)?

options.text: DC would overheat the iron core
AC produces a continuously changing magnetic field, which is needed to induce a voltage in the secondary coil
DC cannot flow through copper wire

questions.explanation: Transformers work by electromagnetic induction, which requires a changing magnetic flux. AC naturally creates a constantly changing current, which produces a constantly changing magnetic field in the iron core. This changing field induces a voltage in the secondary coil. DC produces a steady field with no change, so no voltage is induced.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker and a dynamic microphone both contain a coil and a permanent magnet. What is the key difference in how they work?

options.text: A speaker uses stronger magnets than a microphone
A speaker uses the motor effect (current produces motion) while a microphone uses electromagnetic induction (motion produces current)
A microphone uses DC while a speaker uses AC
A speaker has more coil turns than a microphone

questions.explanation: A loudspeaker uses the motor effect: an alternating current through the coil in a magnetic field creates a force that moves the cone to produce sound. A dynamic microphone uses electromagnetic induction: sound waves move the coil in a magnetic field, inducing an alternating current that represents the sound signal.
